name: Pineal Parenchymal Tumor of Intermediate Differentiation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Histological examination showing intermediate differentiation between pineocytoma and pineoblastoma with moderate cellularity and mitotic activity
Positive immunoreactivity for neuronal markers such as synaptophysin and neurofilament proteins
MRI showing a well-circumscribed pineal region mass with heterogeneous enhancement
Moderate mitotic index (2-5 mitoses per 10 high power fields)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of intermediate differentiation with supportive immunohistochemical and radiological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing may assist but is not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Classic sign due to dorsal midbrain compression
searchTerms: difficulty moving eyes up and down
brain fluid buildup causing eye swelling
pressure in brain with optic nerve swelling

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
common.notes: Often progressive and worse in the morning
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure

common.notes: Often related to sixth nerve involvement
searchTerms: eye movement problems causing double vision

occasional.notes: May occur due to optic pathway compression

occasional.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction (precocious puberty or delayed puberty)
occasional.notes: Rarely due to hypothalamic-pituitary axis involvement
Due to adjacent brain structure involvement

searchTerms: sudden episodes of unstable autonomic functions
episodes of abnormal heart rate and breathing

laboratory: CSF cytology typically negative for malignant cells
imaging: MRI shows well-circumscribed pineal region mass with heterogeneous contrast enhancement
Possible hydrocephalus due to aqueductal stenosis
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; some cases show alterations in DICER1 or other microRNA processing genes
other: Histopathology reveals moderate cellularity with neurocytic differentiation and mitotic activity
Immunohistochemistry positive for synaptophysin, neuron-specific enolase, and variable Ki-67 proliferation index

distinguishingFeatures: Poor differentiation with aggressive clinical course
Presence of germ cell tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG)

redFlags: Signs of acute hydrocephalus (altered consciousness, papilledema)
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Brat DJ, et al. Pineal Parenchymal Tumors: A Review. J Neuropathol Exp Neurol. 2018.
